decision: CPU typing gains did not satisfy the GPU tail guard; the final inactive-path repair also failed its predeclared screen.
limits: All versions used the same production Controls workload and dependencies. CPU slowdown does not emulate a slower GPU.
Input latency starts at the document input listener and ends at an upload acknowledgement; it excludes earlier key processing and display presentation.
Frozen-source validation fields describe each recorded run, not the restored working tree. No rejected timing batch is pooled into an accepted baseline.
The focus and following capture receipts are joined by source/read. The window contains events strictly after the focus receipt through the next same-source receipt.

Direct-text, certification and region events do not carry source/read identity; their association uses this verified single-source workload and ordered window. This analysis does not infer exact capture start times.
fullInputWarmup records scheduling only. Actual first-use avoidance requires directInputText to precede every upstream captureRegion, reused SVG or unchanged-frame operation in the next-read window.
A scheduled warmup that is not first used directly remains a reported miss; no row is filtered.
All740 input acknowledgement→capture receipt→upload joins use exact source/read and upload generation.

captureRegion lacks source/read fields. Its association requires exactly one region or reused-SVG operation between consecutive same-source receipts in the verified single-source workload. Allread windows satisfy it.

The actual captureReadStarted and lastFinishedAt timestamps are absent. Previous receipt+150ms is a receipt-based eligibility floor, not the exact scheduler deadline. Post-floor time includes timer delay, unobserved snapshot work and capture work.

For captureRegion reads, the post-floor interval can be split at the observed region entry. This entry occurs after capture admission and snapshot work; it is not captureReadStarted. Reused-SVG reads have only a ready event, so their start/capture cost cannot be separated.
The unchanged150ms policy is read from a355cc5 rasterizedSource.ts. These inputs have no immediate-refresh bypass; region entries obey the receipt-based floor within1ms.

p95 is the second-largest of37 observed input latencies. Its driving index/read can differ across a pair; own-p95 component differences are descriptive, not a causal same-input comparison. Same-index and same-read-offset comparisons are supplied separately.

Input timing begins at the document listener, after browser event creation. It is not physical-key or CDP-request latency. Event-time differences and typing cadence cannot by themselves establish benchmark feedback as the cause.
